newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends weaker on increased late selling.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends weaker on increased late selling.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
May (3rd pos) 1,275 rgt/tonne Feb (south) 1,337.50
Open/Hi/Low 1,305/1,308/1,275 Prev close 1,347.1Prev
settlement 1,301 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices lost further ground at the close with broad double-digit losses amid talk of a smaller fall in February output. More technical selling emerged after May futures fell below 1,290 ringgit. Next support level was 1,265. Initial prices were marked up on PORLA data.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL- Some hedge selling was also seen, with interest focused on nearby CPOs and selected oils.
Malaysian palm oil prices fell further in late trading and ended weaker on technical and plantation house selling amid talk of a smaller fall in February production, traders said.
More selling emerged when May futures traded below 1,290 ringgit. "People became nervous and started throwing their positions in volatile trade," the trader said.

"Sellers were mostly from commission houses," the trader said, adding that there were some hedge sales from plantation houses. Declines were sharp and double-digit falls were seen across the futures board.
At the close, the May futures contract closed 26 ringgit lower at 1,275 ringgit ($514.73) a tonne.
"Prices fell further in late trading as people are concerned over the output for Febraury," a trader said.
"Some fresh selling came out in late morning trading after people were talking that output in February could be smaller," a trader said.
"People speculated that there were more fruits harvested in recent days as many workers had returned from the long Chinese and Moslem festivals holidays," he said.
However there were no estimates of February's output by traders.
Prices had earlier opened higher, aided by supportive Malaysian official January crop data, traders said.

On Saturday, Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) announced lower-than-expected end-January palm oil stocks of 696,272 tonnes, down from 794,454 tonnes at end-December, and against trade estimates of 710,000-720,000.
"PORLA's numbers are friendly and there was some fresh buying at the opening," a trader said, but he added the market eased thereafter on talk of a smaller fall in February's production.

Physicals Feb (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,337.50 ringgit against bids of 1,325 with earlier trades done at 1,342.50 and 1,340. Feb (central) saw offers at 1,330 and bids at 1,317.50 and Feb (north) at 1,325 against 1,310.
March (south) was offered at 1,337.50 with bids at 1,325 after trading at 1,342.50 and 1,340. March (central) saw offers at 1,325 with bids at 1,312.50.
Among refined products, Mar RBD palm oil was offered at $565 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Apr at $555 and May/Jun at $550.
Mar RBD palm olein saw offers at $587.50, Apr at $580 and May/Jun at $572.50. Apr was traded $585, $580 and $577.50.
Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $467.50 and Mar palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $307.50.
